Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aether Renewables third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aether Renewables' results for the third quarter. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Jane Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Mark Chen, Chief Development Officer; Liam Harper, Chief Technology Officer; and Sara Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong third quarter performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Let me share six key highlights from the quarter. First, we made significant additions to our development pipeline and achieved critical project milestones that reinforce our growth trajectory. Second, our capital expenditures and operating expenses reflected efficient scaling as we advance our construction efforts. Third, we accelerated storage deployments and hybrid project progress, enhancing grid reliability and revenue potential. Fourth, revenue and earnings showed exceptional growth, fueled by higher volumes and margin expansion. Fifth, PPA pricing trends remained favorable, supported by strategic contract extensions that secure long-term cash flows. And sixth, the policy and regulatory environment continues to provide strong tailwinds for our operations.

Now, I will turn the call over to Jane Rivera to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jane Rivera:
Thank you, Elena. We are very pleased with our financial performance in the third quarter. Revenue was $1.45 billion, a 52% increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 29.8%, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $187 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $172 million, or $0.92 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

To give more color on our revenue and earnings growth, this quarter's record $1.45 billion in revenue marked an 18% sequential increase, outperforming our guidance thanks to robust execution amid tailwinds from the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act, Europe's REPowerEU, and tightening supply chains. Adjusted EBITDA reached $285 million, expanding margins to 19.7%, while net income rose 68% year-over-year. Our solar PV segment, representing 55% of revenue at $798 million, grew 61% on 4.2 GWdc shipments, with average selling prices steady at $0.28 per watt due to premiums for our high-efficiency bifacial TOPCon modules qualifying for IRA domestic content credits adding about $0.07 per watt. Energy storage contributed 28% or $406 million, up 72%, from 2.8 GWh deployments leveraging our Nevada gigafactory efficiencies. EPC and O&M services added $246 million, up 35%. North America drove 48% of revenue with 78% growth, Europe 32%, APAC 15%, and LatAm 5%. Earnings benefited from gross margins up 420 basis points to 29.8% via hedged polysilicon at $11 per kilogram and recycled silver paste savings, with OpEx at 8.2% of revenue.

On capital expenditures, we deployed $428 million this quarter, year-to-date $812 million toward our $1.8 to $2.0 billion full-year target, up 15% year-over-year as our 2.5 GW construction pipeline hits 85% mechanical completion. Construction took 72% or $308 million, focused on Southwest U.S. like the 450 MWdc Desert Bloom Phase II, with modules at $0.22 per watt DC from JinkoSolar and LONGi, and EPC at $0.92 per watt. Battery storage CAPEX rose 25% to $85 million for 200 MWh LFP in Texas and iron-air pilots. Land and development was $22 million for Central Valley agrivoltaics. U.S. dominated at 88%, with IRA boosting ITC to 55%. CAPEX per MWdc fell 7% to $1.05 million via vertical integration. For OPEX, $187 million was up 8% year-over-year but flat sequentially, at $14,200 per MW operated across our 4.2 GW fleet at 28.5% capacity factor. O&M was $112 million at $8.50 per kW-year, down 6% with AI predictive maintenance cutting outages to 1.2%. SG&A rose 12% to $42 million for PPA origination, R&D $18 million for perovskites and VPP software. We guide full-year CAPEX to $1.9 billion midpoint and OPEX to $780-820 million.

PPA pricing trends and extensions have been key, with our contracted backlog at 8.2 GW averaging 14 years remaining. Global solar PPAs stabilized at $28-35 per MWh, up 5-8%, wind $32-42, offshore $60-80. In the U.S., ERCOT at $24/MWh with storage adders to $32, CAISO $29, PJM $36. Europe saw dips to €25-30 but UK extensions at €40. APAC like Australia AUD 45/MWh and India ₹2.5/kWh. We extended 1.2 GW with 15% uplifts, like Midwest wind to $34/MWh post-repowering, now 85% contracted through 2035. Looking ahead, prices firm 3-5% in 2025.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark Chen for an update on our project pipeline.

Mark Chen:
Thank you, Jane. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 28.7 GW of projects under development. We are making good progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters. We are also actively exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Diving deeper, in Q3 we added a robust 4.2 GW to our global development pipeline, a 17% quarter-over-quarter increase, placing us in the top quartile with an 8.5x pipeline-to-installed ratio versus our 3.4 GW operating portfolio. By technology: solar PV 2.1 GW including the 1.2 GW Desert Bloom in the U.S. Southwest with N-type TOPCon bifacial at 23.5% efficiency and LCOE below $25/MWh; wind 1.4 GW with 450 MW WindForge onshore in ERCOT at 55% capacity factors using 6 MW Siemens Gamesa turbines, and 250 MW Atlantic Horizon offshore; battery storage 500 MW/1.8 GWh like 300 MW/1.2 GWh Ironclad BESS in California with 90% efficiency, plus 100 MW green hydrogen. U.S. 65% at 2.7 GW, Europe 25%, APAC 10%. We hit 12 de-risking milestones, converting 1.8 GW to advanced: FID on 500 MW Solara Peak solar, NTP on 200 MW WindRidge, permits for 800 MW solar, MISO approval for 400 MW hybrids, grid qual for 50 MW iron-air battery, and $50 million hydrogen grant. Hybridization at 40% boosts IRRs 200-300 bps, corporate LOIs for 2.5 GW, 75% shovel-ready. Q4 adds 3-5 GW, 1 GW FIDs.

Next, Liam Harper will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Liam Harper:
Thank you, Mark. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future. The development of our Apex GridSync AI platform is expected to have a transformative impact on our future projects by optimizing bids and lifting yields by 18%.

On storage deployment and hybrids, we achieved first-year operation on 450 MW/1,800 MWh standalone BESS, totaling 2.3 GW/9.2 GWh operational, up 180% year-over-year. Highlights: 200 MW/800 MWh Horizon Valley in ERCOT with Tesla Megapacks at 92% efficiency generating $28 million EBITDA; 150 MW/600 MWh Sunridge Peak in CAISO with $65/kW-month RA; 100 MW/400 MWh Outback Frontier in Australia. Construction pipeline 1.8 GW/7.2 GWh, capex $220/kWh down 15%, margins 65-70% with IRA 45X credits. Hybrids now 65% of 15 GW pipeline: 400 MWac Eagle Solar Hybrid in PJM at $55/MWh PPA and 42% capacity factor; 250 MW Gale Winds Hybrid in UK at £49.50/MWh CfD. U.S. 70%, Europe advancing 500 MW in Spain. Pioneering iron-air pilots, Samsung SDI partnerships, Ørsted JV for offshore. Storage/hybrids drove $185 million EBITDA, up 220%, reaffirming 1.5 GW storage and 2 GW hybrids COD in FY24.

And now, Sara Patel will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Sara Patel:
Thank you, Liam. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense.

The policy and regulatory environment is a massive tailwind. In the U.S., IRA has spurred $120 billion investments; our 8.2 GW pipeline stacks 30% ITC plus 10% domestic content, monetizing $450 million PTCs. FERC 2223 prioritizes our projects, Section 301 tariffs boost margins 320 bps. Europe: NZIA targets 40 GW manufacturing, our Poland fab gets €150 million; CBAM favors us at €25/MWh LCOE. APAC: India PLI JV with Adani for 10 GW. We're advocating for reforms, modeling 15% policy uplift.

I'll now turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sara. In closing, we are confident that Aether Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question, John. The regulatory landscape is strongly supportive. In the U.S., IRA continues driving growth with ITC/PTC stacking and transferability, our Arizona and Texas fabs qualifying for domestic bonuses amid 50% tariffs on Asian cells. FERC Order 2023 and BLM fast-tracks have de-risked 2.5 GW. Europe accelerates via REPowerEU, NZIA grants, and RED III for PPAs; CBAM protects our supply chain. APAC leverages India's PLI and Australia's mandates. We've hedged against risks like queues and elections with diversified revenue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Liam Harper:
Great question, Maria. Storage integration is core via hybrids comprising 65% of pipeline, with AI like GridSync for 98% LMP forecasting across ISOs. Our 2.3 GW/9.2 GWh operational fleet captures arbitrage, RA, and ancillaries; construction 1.8 GW at declining $220/kWh costs. Pilots in iron-air and flow batteries for long-duration, partnerships with Tesla, Fluence, Form Energy, Samsung. This stacks revenues, boosts capacity factors to 42%, and meets mandates like Chile's 30%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

Elena Vasquez:
David, we're optimistic. BNEF forecasts $1.7 trillion global investment through 2030, with U.S. 35 GW solar in 2025, hybrids dominating per NREL. Our 28.7 GW pipeline at 8.5x ratio, IRA/REPowerEU tailwinds, falling LCOE to $22/MWh unsubsidized, and diversification into hydrogen position us for 10 GW annual deployments through 2028, 25-30% EBITDA growth.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Aether Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
